question: Which of the following instruments is primarily used by the RBI for monetary policy implementation in the post 1991 reform era? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (12/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Repo rate
Export incentives
Tariff rates
Direct taxes
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Repo rate

Explanation:
After the 1991 economic reforms, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) adopted more market-oriented monetary policy instruments. The Repo rate is the rate at which RBI lends short-term funds to commercial banks, and it has become the primary tool for monetary policy implementation. By adjusting the repo rate, RBI controls liquidity in the banking system and targets inflation. Other options like export incentives, tariff rates, and direct taxes fall under fiscal or trade policy, not monetary policy. Changes in the repo rate influence interest rates, borrowing, and overall economic activity.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Repo rate → Rate at which RBI lends to banks overnight
☛ Reverse repo rate → Rate at which RBI absorbs excess liquidity from banks
☛ CRR → Banks must keep a portion of deposits with RBI
☛ SLR → Banks must invest a portion of deposits in government securities
☛ MSF → Banks can borrow from RBI at a higher rate in emergencies
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा उपकरण मुख्य रूप से आरबीआई द्वारा 1991 के बाद के सुधार युग में मौद्रिक नीति कार्यान्वयन के लिए उपयोग किया जाता है? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (12/08/2025) Shift 1)
options_hi: रेपो दर
निर्यात प्रोत्साहन
टैरिफ दरें
प्रत्यक्ष कर
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है रेपो दर

Explanation:
1991 के आर्थिक सुधारों के बाद, भारतीय रिज़र्व बैंक (RBI) ने मौद्रिक नीति को अधिक बाजार-उन्मुख बनाया। रेपो दर वह दर है जिस पर RBI वाणिज्यिक बैंकों को अल्पकालिक ऋण देता है, और यह मौद्रिक नीति का प्रमुख उपकरण बन गया है। इसके माध्यम से RBI बैंकिंग प्रणाली में तरलता को नियंत्रित करता है और मुद्रास्फीति को लक्षित करता है। अन्य विकल्प जैसे निर्यात प्रोत्साहन, टैरिफ दरें और प्रत्यक्ष कर राजकोषीय नीति या व्यापार नीति के अंतर्गत आते हैं, मौद्रिक नीति के नहीं। रेपो दर में बदलाव से ब्याज दरें, ऋण और समग्र आर्थिक गतिविधियां प्रभावित होती हैं।

question: Which economic system dominated India on the eve of independence (in 1947)? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (12/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Import substitution industrialisation
Colonial agrarian economy
Global free market
Socialist planned economy
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Colonial agrarian economy

Explanation:
On the eve of independence in 1947, India's economy was predominantly a colonial agrarian economy, with about 70% of the population dependent on agriculture. British rule turned India into a supplier of raw materials and a market for finished goods. Modern industry was very limited, and the land revenue system exploited peasants. A socialist planned economy was adopted later, while import substitution industrialization began in the 1950s. The global free market was implemented after 1991.

☛ How did British rule treat India? → As a supplier of raw materials
☛ When was socialist planned economy adopted in India? → In the 1950s
☛ When did import substitution industrialization start? → In the 1950s
☛ When was the global free market policy implemented in India? → After 1991

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है औपनिवेशिक कृषि अर्थव्यवस्था

Explanation:
1947 में स्वतंत्रता के समय भारत की अर्थव्यवस्था मुख्यतः औपनिवेशिक कृषि प्रधान थी, जिसमें लगभग 70% जनसंख्या कृषि पर निर्भर थी। ब्रिटिश शासन ने भारत को कच्चे माल का आपूर्तिकर्ता और तैयार माल का बाजार बना दिया था। आधुनिक उद्योग बहुत सीमित थे, और भू-राजस्व व्यवस्था ने किसानों का शोषण किया। समाजवादी नियोजित अर्थव्यवस्था बाद में अपनाई गई, जबकि आयात प्रतिस्थापन 1950 के दशक में शुरू हुआ। वैश्विक मुक्त बाजार 1991 के बाद लागू हुआ।

question: The primary sector saw uneven regional development during 1947-91. Which region benefitted the most from the Green Revolution? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (12/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Western India
Eastern India
Northern India
Southern India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Northern India

Explanation:
The Green Revolution, initiated in the 1960s, focused on high-yielding variety seeds, fertilizers, and irrigation. The region that benefitted the most was Northern India, particularly the states of Punjab, Haryana, and western Uttar Pradesh. These areas had access to canal irrigation and fertile alluvial plains, which facilitated the adoption of modern farming techniques. Crop production, especially wheat and rice, increased significantly. In contrast, Eastern and Southern India saw limited benefits due to inadequate irrigation infrastructure and fragmented landholdings.

☛ Which crops were the focus of the Green Revolution? → Wheat and Rice
☛ Which state is known as the 'Food Bowl of India'? → Punjab
☛ In which decade did the Green Revolution start? → 1960s
☛ From where were high-yielding variety seeds imported? → Mexico (wheat) and Philippines (rice)

question: A mixed economy involves both private and public ownership. What was a distinctive feature of India's mixed economy model? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (12/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Public sector dominance in core industries
Absence of licensing
Full privatisation
Focus on consumerism
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Public sector dominance in core industries

Explanation:
India's mixed economy model was characterized by the coexistence of public and private sectors, but its distinctive feature was the dominance of the public sector in core industries such as steel, energy, and railways. This was aimed at establishing a socialist society and controlling economic development. The government regulated the private sector through licensing and quota systems. This model was based on the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956.

☛ Main objective of public sector in mixed economy → Control of basic industries
☛ When did the licensing system end? → In the 1991 economic reforms
☛ Largest public sector industry in India → Railways
☛ When was private sector allowed in core industries? → After 1991

question: Which of the following options best describes the state of Indian industries under British rule? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (12/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Promotion of indigenous entrepreneurship
Rapid growth of modern manufacturing
Widespread industrialisation across rural India
Systematic decline of traditional industries
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Systematic decline of traditional industries

Explanation:
Under British rule, the state of Indian industries is best described as the systematic decline of traditional industries. The British used India as a source of raw materials and a market for finished goods. They deliberately implemented policies to destroy Indian handicrafts and textile industries, such as high tariffs and free entry of British machine-made goods. Consequently, traditional industrial centers like Surat, Murshidabad, and Dhaka were devastated. British policies aimed at weakening Indian industries, not promoting them. Modern manufacturing was limited to a few sectors, and widespread industrialization did not occur in rural India. Thus, the decline of traditional industries was a deliberate strategy of British rule.

☛ Consequence of decline of traditional Indian industries → Increased unemployment and poverty
☛ Which industry survived under British rule → Some agro-based industries

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है पारंपरिक उद्योगों का व्यवस्थित पतन

Explanation:
ब्रिटिश शासन के दौरान भारतीय उद्योगों की स्थिति का सबसे सटीक वर्णन पारंपरिक उद्योगों का व्यवस्थित पतन है। अंग्रेजों ने भारत को कच्चे माल के स्रोत और तैयार माल के बाजार के रूप में इस्तेमाल किया। उन्होंने भारतीय हस्तशिल्प और वस्त्र उद्योगों को नष्ट करने के लिए जानबूझकर नीतियां बनाईं, जैसे कि उच्च कर और ब्रिटिश मशीन-निर्मित वस्तुओं का मुफ्त प्रवेश। परिणामस्वरूप, सूरत, मुर्शिदाबाद और ढाका जैसे पारंपरिक औद्योगिक केंद्र तबाह हो गए। ब्रिटिश नीतियों का उद्देश्य भारतीय उद्योगों को कमजोर करना था, न कि उन्हें बढ़ावा देना। आधुनिक विनिर्माण केवल कुछ क्षेत्रों तक सीमित रहा, और ग्रामीण भारत में औद्योगीकरण नहीं हुआ। इस प्रकार, पारंपरिक उद्योगों का पतन ब्रिटिश शासन की एक जानबूझकर की गई रणनीति थी।

question: Tariff reforms were central to the liberalisation of trade. What happened to import tariffs after 1991? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (12/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: It increased
It gradually reduced
It remained unchanged
It was replaced with import bans
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is It gradually reduced

Explanation:
After the economic reforms of 1991, India adopted trade liberalization policies aimed at reducing import tariffs to integrate with the global economy. In 1990-91, the average tariff rate was around 80%, which was gradually reduced to below 15% by the 2000s. This reduction was implemented in phases, making imports more accessible and increasing competition in the domestic market. Lower tariffs benefited consumers with cheaper and diverse products, while domestic industries faced pressure to improve efficiency. The tariff reforms were crucial in promoting economic growth, attracting foreign investment, and enhancing India's competitiveness in international trade. The gradual reduction helped in a smooth transition, avoiding sudden shocks to the economy.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ What happened to import tariffs after 1991 reforms? → Gradually reduced
☛ What was the average tariff rate in 1990-91? → Around 80%
☛ What was the average tariff rate by the 2000s? → Below 15%
☛ What was the main objective of reducing tariffs? → To integrate with global economy and increase competition
☛ What was a benefit of lower tariffs? → Consumers got cheaper products and foreign investment increased
question_hi: व्यापार के उदारीकरण के लिए टैरिफ सुधार केंद्रीय थे। 1991 के बाद आयात टैरिफ का क्या हुआ? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (12/08/2025) Shift 2)

question: Privatisation under the 1991 reforms primarily involved: (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (12/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: increasing agricultural subsidies
reducing bank interest rates
nationalising private companies
selling government shares in public sector enterprises
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is selling government shares in public sector enterprises

Explanation:
Privatisation under the 1991 economic reforms primarily involved the sale of government stakes in public sector undertakings (PSUs) to the private sector. This reduced government ownership and control, aiming to improve efficiency, foster competition, and reduce fiscal deficits. It was a key pillar of the New Economic Policy (NEP) 1991, along with liberalisation and globalisation. Increasing agricultural subsidies or reducing bank interest rates are separate policy measures, not part of privatisation. Nationalisation (bringing private companies under government control) is the opposite of privatisation. The disinvestment process began gradually, with the government selling minority stakes in many PSUs to raise revenue and enhance performance.

question: Which of the following is an example of structural unemployment?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (13/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: A worker choosing not to work due to a lack of job opportunities
A worker being unable to find a job due to discrimination
A worker losing their job due to a recession
A worker being unable to find a job due to a lack of skills in a new and expanding industry
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is A worker being unable to find a job due to a lack of skills in a new and expanding industry.

Explanation:
Structural unemployment arises from long-term changes in the economy, such as technological advancements or the decline of industries. When workers lack the skills required for available jobs in growing sectors, they experience structural unemployment. Option 4 clearly illustrates this: a worker cannot find a job because they lack skills for a new and expanding industry. Other options: Option 1 is voluntary unemployment, Option 2 is discrimination-related (possibly structural but not the best example), and Option 3 is cyclical unemployment. Thus, the correct answer highlights skill mismatch as a cause of structural unemployment.

☛ Cyclical unemployment is related to → Business cycles and recessions

☛ Example of voluntary unemployment → Worker choosing not to work due to low wages
☛ Unemployment due to discrimination → Can be a form of structural unemployment

Explanation:

question: India’s foreign trade structure changed significantly under British rule. During the colonial period, what kind of goods did India primarily export? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (14/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Capital goods
Manufactured goods
Automobiles
Raw materials
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Raw materials

Explanation:
Under British rule, India's foreign trade structure was completely transformed. India was turned into an exporter of raw materials and an importer of British manufactured goods. India primarily exported raw materials such as cotton, jute, tea, indigo, oilseeds, and minerals. These raw materials were sent to British factories, where they were processed into finished goods and then sold back to India. This policy was designed to serve British industrial interests, leading to the deindustrialization of India and making it a mere supplier of raw materials. The colonial trade structure caused economic drain and hindered India's industrial development, keeping the economy dependent on agriculture.

question: Who is considered unemployed under the Usual Status (US) measure? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (14/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Someone working only one day a week
Someone retired from work
Someone not working but seeking work over a long period
Someone working part-time
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Someone not working but seeking work over a long period

Explanation:
The Usual Status (US) measure is a key employment indicator used by India's National Sample Survey Office (NSSO). It refers to a person's principal activity based on the majority of time spent over the past 365 days. Under this measure, an individual is considered unemployed if they are not working and have been actively seeking work over a long period. Option 3 matches this definition. Options 1 and 4 describe persons who are employed (even if for fewer hours), while Option 2 (retired) is outside the labor force. The US measure captures chronic unemployment rather than short-term or seasonal joblessness. It helps analyze long-term labor market trends and policy impacts.

☛ Who is excluded from US measure? → Retired, students, and persons engaged in domestic duties
☛ What reference period does US use? → Principal activity over past 365 days
☛ Difference between US and CWS? → CWS measures weekly status, US covers annual activity
☛ What does NSSO stand for? → National Sample Survey Office, which collects employment data

question: Which of the following is considered a major social development outcome of India’s economic reforms since 1991?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (14/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Increase in poverty rate
Widening of fiscal deficit
Decrease in literacy rate
Improvement in life expectancy
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Improvement in life expectancy

Explanation:
The economic reforms of 1991 accelerated India's economic growth, leading to expanded access to healthcare services and a significant improvement in life expectancy. Post-reforms, both public and private healthcare infrastructure expanded. This resulted in reduced infant mortality and improved nutrition, raising the average life expectancy from about 58 years in 1990 to approximately 70 years by 2020. This is considered a major social development outcome. Other options—increase in poverty rate, widening of fiscal deficit, and decrease in literacy rate—are not outcomes of the reforms; in fact, poverty declined, the fiscal deficit was controlled, and literacy increased.

☛ Poverty rate change → declined from 45% (1993-94) to 22% (2011-12)
☛ Healthcare expansion → increased private sector participation
☛ Infant mortality rate → declined from 88 per 1000 (1990) to 28 per 1000 (2020)

question: Post-independence, India adopted a planned approach to build a mixed economy. Which sector was given top priority under the First Five-Year Plan? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (14/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Agriculture
Tertiary
Defence
Industry
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Agriculture

Explanation:
After independence, India adopted a planned approach under the mixed economy model. The First Five-Year Plan (1951–56) gave top priority to agriculture due to severe food grain shortages and the sector's dominant role in the economy. Its main objectives were to increase food production and reduce import dependence. The plan emphasized multi-purpose river projects (e.g., Bhakra-Nangal) and land reforms. It was successful, achieving a GDP growth rate of 3.6% against a target of 2.1%. Later plans shifted focus to industry.

question: Which type of unemployment is most prevalent in Indian agriculture during the nonsowing season?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (18/08/2025) Shift 1)

Seasonal Unemployment
Disguised Unemployment
Structural Unemployment
solution:

Explanation:
In Indian agriculture, Seasonal Unemployment is most prevalent during the nonsowing season. This type of unemployment occurs due to the seasonal nature of agricultural activities, where labor demand is high during sowing and harvesting seasons but low during other months. question: What is a key indicator of economic growth that has shown sustained improvement in India since 1991? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (18/08/2025) Shift 2)

question: Which sector dominated India's national income before independence? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (18/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Industry
Agriculture
Trade and transport
Banking
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Agriculture

Explanation:
Before independence, the Indian economy was predominantly agrarian. About 70-75% of the population depended on agriculture, and its contribution to national income was over 50%. The industrial sector was underdeveloped, while trade and banking sectors were limited in scope. During British rule, India experienced de-industrialization, which further increased dependence on agriculture. Agricultural techniques were backward, and social structures like the zamindari system worsened the condition of farmers. Thus, agriculture dominated India's national income before independence.

question: Which of the following statements correctly describes India's foreign trade structure at the time of independence? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (18/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Balanced trade
Complete trade isolation
High export of finished goods
Export of raw materials and import of manufactured goods.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Export of raw materials and import of manufactured goods.

Explanation:
At the time of independence, India's foreign trade structure reflected colonial exploitation. The British turned India into an exporter of raw materials (like cotton, jute, tea) and an importer of finished goods (like textiles, machinery) from Britain. This unbalanced trade weakened Indian industries. Under British policy, India conducted most of its imports from Britain, while exports were mainly agricultural and mineral products. Export of finished goods was minimal and trade balance was not in India's favor. Thus, the correct option indicates that India exported raw materials and imported manufactured goods.

question: The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) was established to formalise inflation targeting. How many members constitute India’s MPC? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (18/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: 6
3
5
7
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 6

Explanation:
The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) in India was established in 2016 to formalize inflation targeting. The MPC consists of 6 members: 3 from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) - the Governor (Chairperson), a Deputy Governor in charge of monetary policy, and one RBI official; and 3 external experts appointed by the central government. The primary function of the MPC is to set the repo rate to maintain inflation at the target of 4% (with a tolerance band of 2% to 6%). Decisions are taken by majority vote, and the Governor has the casting vote in case of a tie.

भारत में मौद्रिक नीति समिति (MPC) की स्थापना वर्ष 2016 में की गई थी, जिसका उद्देश्य मुद्रास्फीति लक्ष्यीकरण को औपचारिक रूप देना था। MPC में कुल 6 सदस्य होते हैं, जिनमें से 3 सदस्य भारतीय रिज़र्व बैंक (RBI) के होते हैं - गवर्नर (अध्यक्ष), डिप्टी गवर्नर (मौद्रिक नीति प्रभारी), और RBI के एक अधिकारी। शेष 3 सदस्य बाहरी विशेषज्ञ होते हैं जिन्हें केंद्र सरकार द्वारा नियुक्त किया जाता है। MPC का प्रमुख कार्य रेपो दर तय करना है ताकि मुद्रास्फीति को 4% के लक्ष्य (सहिष्णुता सीमा 2% से 6%) पर बनाए रखा जा सके। निर्णय बहुमत से लिए जाते हैं, और गवर्नर के पास निर्णायक मत होता है।

question: The drain of wealth theory was a major critique of colonial economic policies. Who propounded the ‘Drain of wealth theory’ in the late 19th century?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (19/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Dadabhai Naoroji
Mahatma Gandhi
Gopal Krishna Gokhale
Jawaharlal Nehru
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Dadabhai Naoroji

Explanation:
The Drain of Wealth Theory was propounded by Dadabhai Naoroji, a prominent Indian nationalist and economist. He elaborated this theory in his seminal book "Poverty and Un-British Rule in India" (1901). According to this theory, during British rule, India's wealth was continuously drained to Britain, leading to India's impoverishment. Naoroji argued that British colonial policies were detrimental to India's economic interests and resulted in a massive outflow of wealth from the country. This theory became a cornerstone of the economic critique of British imperialism and significantly influenced the Indian independence movement.

solution_hi:

Explanation:
धन निष्कासन सिद्धांत के प्रतिपादक दादाभाई नौरोजी थे, जो एक प्रमुख भारतीय राष्ट्रवादी और अर्थशास्त्री थे। उन्होंने अपनी पुस्तक "पॉवर्टी एंड अन-ब्रिटिश रूल इन इंडिया" (1901) में इस सिद्धांत को विस्तार से समझाया। इस सिद्धांत के अनुसार, ब्रिटिश शासन के दौरान भारत की संपत्ति लगातार ब्रिटेन में स्थानांतरित होती रही, जिससे भारत गरीब हुआ। नौरोजी ने यह तर्क दिया कि ब्रिटिश नीतियां भारत के आर्थिक हितों के विपरीत थीं और इससे देश से भारी मात्रा में धन का बहिर्गमन हुआ। यह सिद्धांत भारतीय स्वतंत्रता आंदोलन की आर्थिक आलोचना का एक मुख्य आधार बना।
